page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates four dedicated virtual CPUs across two physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB, establishing a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 with VNNI, AES-NI, and FMA, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. The server does not bundle local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, and it provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in the lower quartile across several raw compute and memory metrics, balanced by moderate single-threaded responsiveness. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1166.0, situated in the middle performance tier, alongside a multi-core score of 2549.0. Stress-ng scores show 1310.68 for single-core and 3484.23 for multi-core compute throughput. Memory bandwidth tests record 26.23 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.85 GB/sec for writes. Application-level evaluations indicate a Redis SET throughput of 3.38 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 3.84 GB/sec.

The 1:2 memory profile provides an entry-level compute footprint for workloads where extensive memory arrays are unnecessary. Because there is no bundled local storage, persistent disk operations rely entirely on attached network block storage, which shares the host I/O pipeline with the 2 Gbps baseline network interface. This configuration fits standard microservices, lightweight web servers, continuous integration tasks, and intermediate batch processing pipelines that prioritize compute cycles over high data persistence throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor on the KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It includes no bundled local storage and zero GPU accelerators, requiring remote block storage for data persistence. Benchmark evaluations show balanced single-core performance with a Geekbench score of 1166.0, alongside lower-tier multi-threaded and memory metrics such as a 2549.0 Geekbench multi-core score and 26.23 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector extensions and 35 MB of L3 cache. With its 1:2 memory-to-core allocation, ecs.c6.xlarge is designed for lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, batch processing, and compute-focused microservices that do not require high memory density.
